profile.preferences: I want fresh, untouched powder, wherever that exists. Trees, bowls, steeps, flatter terrain, whatever. I have a bit of a preference for steeper terrain when the powder gets truly deep, and less steep/cruisier terrain on more mild amount of powder.
profile.provenance: Restored preference text from older Powder Hunter profile, which has no historical version timestamp. Standardized benchmark assumption; absent from newer database. This is not an exact historical profile replay.

travel_value.user_statement: Around $800 for a short Cascades trip would be worthwhile for exceptionally deep days with confirmed road and resort access. $1,700 sounds expensive; investigate a shorter or cheaper practical trip rather than anchoring on that estimate.
travel_value.interpretation: A value reference, not a hard maximum, verified quote, or requirement that every trip cost $800.

aformentioned low pressure system moves through. Expect 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms along the Uinta 
Mountains Thursday afternoon, with precipitation pushing 
southeast Thursday night into Friday morning. 

Snow levels drop on Friday as a strong cold front traverses the

mountains, with light snow possible in the valleys as well. As 
of now accumulations do not look impressive, but periods of 
winter travel conditions cannot be ruled out, especially at pass
level. We will need moderate the heavy snowfall rates in the 
valleys in order to see accumulating snow on the warm pavement, 
which is only possible as the cold front is moving through. 

Perhaps most importantly, a hard freeze very likely Friday 
night into Saturday morning as this system moves off to the 
east. Many of the valleys across the region will see lows in the
teens to upper 20's. Freeze Watches have been issued as we gear
up for this impactful event. 

LOOKING AHEAD:

A ridge of high pressure builds back in this weekend into early
next week resulting in the return of unseasonably warm 
temperatures.

reference.rationale: Skip the currently described lift-served trip if season-ending closures persist through the visit. Distinguish seasonal shutdown from temporary closure; consider a credible bonus reopening or open alternative if evidence supports it.
must_address: Identify whether closure is seasonal or temporary and whether any credible reopening overlaps a reachable ski day; do not equate closed today with no future opportunity.
Distinguish expected snowfall from accessible skiing.
Do not pivot to backcountry based only on expert resort skill.
A possible reopening is a condition to verify, not a promised itinerary.
Do not invent a reopening, but do not dismiss a supported reopening or practical open-resort alternative.
